title: On some perfect matching conjectures in infinite, cubic, bridgeless graphs
summary: The Berge-Fulkerson Conjecture states that every bridgeless cubic graph has six perfect matchings such that each edge belongs to exactly two of them. This conjecture has remained open since 1971, and several of its weakenings have been proposed over the years. Two of the most prominent are the Fan-Raspaud Conjecture and the Máčajová-Škoviera Conjecture. It is well known that the Berge-Fulkerson Conjecture implies the Fan-Raspaud Conjecture, which in turn implies the Máčajová-Škoviera Conjecture.
